dedupe_keys.name: anuga shallow water flood and tsunami model

description: ANUGA is open-source software that solves the two-dimensional shallow water equations and is used in particular to model floods and tsunamis, including dam-break flows and inundation behind or around flood defences. It represents the study area as a mesh of triangular cells and uses a finite-volume scheme, so wetting and drying, complex terrain and hydraulic structures can be simulated. Geoscience Australia and the Mathematical Sciences Institute of the Australian National University created it; a community of volunteers now develops and maintains it, with the most up-to-date Python 3 version in the anuga-community repository and a mirror at Geoscience Australia (a Python 2.7 branch remains for legacy users). It is a Python 3 package with C and Cython extensions and an optional Fortran extension, installable from PyPI (version 4.0.1 of 17 September 2026) or conda-forge, or run in a preconfigured cloud workspace; documentation is on Read the Docs. The PyPI record gives the Apache-2.0 licence and it is free of charge. It is site-independent: users supply elevation, boundary conditions and structures for any location. Caveats: building a good mesh and calibrating roughness need expertise, and large domains need parallel runs. Simulation uses: flood and dam-break hazard exposure, tsunami inundation, emergency planning and climate adaptation of flood defences and urban drainage. It is an open alternative to HEC-RAS 2D (model-hec-ras) for two-dimensional inundation modelling.
